summary.title: From Skills to Talent: Organising Heterogeneous Agents as a Real-World Company

details: Multi-agent LLM systems are limited by fixed team composition, backend-specific coupling, prompt-described (non-executable) roles, and session-bound learning; there is no organisational layer separating how a workforce is assembled/governed/improved from what individual agents know.

OneManCompany (OMC): an open-source framework that treats the AI 'company' as the unit of design, built on (i) Employee = Talent (portable agent identity: prompts, role, skills, tools) + Container (runtime backend), mediated by six typed organisational interfaces (execution, task queue, event bus, storage, context, lifecycle) so heterogeneous agent runtimes coexist, plus a community-driven Talent Market for on-demand hiring.

(ii) Explore-Execute-Review (E^2R) tree search: an MCTS-structured (but rollout-free, real-execution) loop where a supervising agent decomposes tasks top-down into a task tree with DAG dependency edges, agents execute leaves, and accept/reject review signals propagate bottom-up, triggering re-decomposition; AND-tree semantics plus a task finite state machine yield termination, deadlock-freedom and crash-recovery invariants.

(iii) Self-evolution at both levels: agents rewrite working principles via CEO one-on-ones and post-task reflection; project retrospectives distil SOPs, and an HR pipeline (periodic reviews, PIP, automated offboarding) replaces underperformers from the Talent Market.

Search tree T=(V, E_tree, E_dep) with node state (task desc, assigned employee, FSM status, result, cost) plus shared workforce/resource state; five action types: decompose, assign, recruit, review, iterate.
FSM with 9 states (pending, processing, holding, completed, accepted, failed, blocked, finished, cancelled); completed->accepted requires explicit supervisor review; bounded retries.

Seven stated invariants (DAG acyclicity at insertion, mutual exclusion |running(e)|<=1, schedule idempotency, review termination, cascade completeness, dependency completeness, recovery correctness); bounded-rationality circuit breakers: review-round limit k_rev=3, task timeout 3600s, cost budget pause.

Human CEO acts as external oracle (policy override, requirement injection, iteration triggering); policy pi is realised by a supervising LLM agent (COO/senior employee), not a learned parameterised policy.

Three supported Container families: LangGraph/LangChain agents, Claude Code CLI sessions, script-based executors; tools exposed uniformly (via MCP for Claude Code) with role/permission-gated registry.
Founding team bootstrapped per instance: HR, Executive Assistant, COO, CSO.

Talent Market with three sourcing channels: curated open-source repo agents, prompt-sourced personas (e.g. Agency-Agents, 140+ personas) auto-assembled with skills from SkillsMP, and fully dynamic skill-assembled agents; shortlist mixed ~80/20 and approved by the human CEO.

PRDBench: 50 project-level software tasks across 20+ domains, official DEV mode (one-shot PRD input, no iterative feedback), scored by automated evaluation scripts; metric = success rate, plus reported dollar cost.

OMC configuration: LangGraph founding agent on Gemini Flash Lite Preview plus three Talent-Market hires (Software Engineer with 'superpowers' plugin, Software Architect, Code Reviewer, all Claude Code-based).
Baselines: PRDBench-reported minimal agents (GPT-5.2, Claude-4.5, Gemini-3-Pro, Qwen3-Coder, DeepSeek-V3.2, etc.) and commercial coding agents (CodeX, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code).

Four single-prompt projects: GitHub AI-agent weekly trend report emailed to the CEO (GPT-4o researcher + Claude Sonnet 4 writer, <10 min, ~$4.48); street-fight web game with human evaluator feedback (Claude Sonnet 4 + Gemini 2.5 with NanoBanana); illustrated audiobook of Peaky Blinders (Novel Writer + Gemini 3.1 Pro AV Producer, 16 scenes, $1.57); autonomous survey on world models (3 Claude Sonnet 4.6 / self-hosted specialists, <1 hour, $16.26, 15.9M tokens, 17 documents, ~70-node mind map, 3 research proposals).
Human involvement limited to the initial prompt plus approving the HR shortlist (and, for the game, external evaluator feedback).

Architectural comparison table vs MetaGPT/ChatDev, AutoGen/LangGraph, CrewAI/Agno, OpenHands, AIOS, AgentScope, Paperclip along agent contract, multi-family execution, agent sourcing, and self/organisational evolution.
Authors note evaluation is confined to PRDBench and that self-evolution mechanisms are deployed but not quantitatively ablated; adaptive dispatch added to route simple tasks to a single agent.

key_findings.finding: OMC sets a new state of the art on the project-level PRDBench under single-attempt zero-shot conditions.
key_findings.evidence: 84.67% success rate versus the best reported baseline Claude-4.5 at 69.19% (+15.48 points), with commercial agents CodeX at 62.09% and Claude Code at 56.65%; total cost $345.59 over 50 tasks (~$6.91/task), and baseline costs were not reported so no efficiency comparison is possible.

key_findings.finding: Decoupling agent identity (Talent) from runtime (Container) via six typed interfaces lets agents from incompatible families be recruited and coordinated inside one project without framework changes.
key_findings.evidence: The PRDBench run mixed a LangGraph Gemini founding agent with three Claude Code Talents hired mid-project from the Talent Market; the four case studies mixed GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4/4.6, Gemini 2.5/3.1 Pro and a self-hosted agent, and the authors report no framework modification was required for any domain.

key_findings.finding: Formal execution guarantees can be attached to a dynamically expanding task tree, which no compared system provides.
key_findings.evidence: AND-tree semantics with a 9-state FSM, DAG cycle detection at insertion, bounded retries and circuit breakers (k_rev=3, 3600s timeout, cost budget), plus a deadlock detector, are argued to give termination, deadlock freedom, cascade cancellation and crash recovery under bounded retry and finite resources; the architectural comparison table shows no prior system offering such guarantees under runtime tree expansion.

key_findings.finding: An enforced completed->accepted review gate plus re-decomposition on rejection gives an error-correction loop that can create new capabilities rather than patch outputs.
key_findings.evidence: In the game-development case study, an external evaluator rejected the build because sprite sheets were unsegmented; the COO/EA re-entered the explore stage and authored a new sprite-slicing skill for the Art Designer, after which assets were regenerated and re-integrated successfully.

key_findings.finding: A one-sentence brief can drive fully autonomous, verifiable multi-stage delivery across non-coding domains at low cost.
key_findings.evidence: The research-survey project produced 17 documents, a ~70-node mind map over 35+ papers, and three grounded research proposals in under an hour for $16.26 (15.9M tokens); the audiobook produced 16 illustrated scenes with narration and two composed videos for $1.57; authors manually verified that cited papers and all GitHub links/star counts in the trend report were real.
